The study uses molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the interaction of paired edge dislocations with cuboidal γ' precipitates in a γ matrix.
The volume fraction of the γ' precipitates is varied from 1% to 60%.
The CRSS for dislocation motion exhibits a power law dependence on the volume fraction of the γ' precipitates, with two distinct regimes separated by a critical precipitate size of around 120 Å.
The 120 Å critical precipitate size corresponds to the total core width of the paired dislocations in the γ' phase, including the complex stacking faults and anti-phase boundary.
The CRSS scales linearly with the length of the γ' precipitate along the direction of dislocation motion, rather than just its volume fraction.
The two-regime power law behavior is observed across a wide range of temperatures (300-700 K), indicating that it is not a thermally activated mechanism.
Simulations with spherical precipitates also exhibit the same two-regime power law behavior, with the transition occurring at the same critical length scale of 120 Å.
The dislocation velocities in the γ and γ' phases are similar, with the velocity in the γ phase being slightly higher than that in the γ' phase.
The variations in the dislocation core width are more dramatic in the first regime (L_γ' < 120 Å) than in the second regime (L_γ' > 120 Å).
The power law exponent b in the CRSS-volume fraction relationship is approximately 0.36 in the first regime and 0.27-0.36 in the second regime.
The current study is limited to the case of γ' precipitates with orientations identical to the γ phase, and future work should explore the effect of different relative orientations.
The findings of this study have important implications for developing predictive models of mechanical behavior and informing alloy design strategies for Ni-based superalloys.
The study provides new computational evidence of a size-dependent strengthening effect in Ni-based superalloys, which has not been previously reported in the literature.

The results highlight the importance of considering the interplay between precipitate size, volume fraction, and other related factors in understanding the strengthening mechanisms in Ni-based superalloys.
The identification of the critical length scale of 120 Å, corresponding to the total dislocation core width, provides a new insight into the size-dependent strengthening behavior in these materials.
